$schema-note: The machine-readable register of every semantic (surface, foreground) pair in the tier-2
role layer, and the contrast each pair is required to hold. It is DATA, consumed by three
gates, and it is the reason a new surface cannot ship without its contrast assertion:
every pair in the BUILT app, and also proves each
role generates a real Tailwind utility.
frontend/tests/e2e/rebrand-drill.spec.ts  re-measures every pair with tier 1 swapped to
tests/test_content_drift.py            asserts index.css declares exactly the roles listed
here — no undeclared surface, no orphan manifest row.
Why pairs and not a flat colour list: a foreground is only legible RELATIVE to a surface, so

AAA-body.why: The two running-copy pairings. This is a reading tool and both surfaces carry body text, so they clear AAA with room. These two thresholds are carried over verbatim from the UI-SPEC 5.5 anchor table.

graphical.why: WCAG non-text contrast: a mark that carries meaning but is not read.

non-text.why: Hairlines and dashed marks ONLY. The upper bound is the assertion: raise a hairline colour to text contrast and the hairlines it draws stop reading as hairlines. The lower bound keeps it visible.

surfaces.what: The top bar and the left rail — the app's own furniture.

foregrounds.what: Body and label copy on the chrome.
Secondary copy on the chrome — inactive nav, footnotes.
Decoration only: separator glyphs.
A link on the chrome is the foreground colour: the accent is PROHIBITED here.
The secondary accent, dark-surface form.

surfaces.what: Cards, panes, popovers, the ledger — the working surface, where the reviewer's eyes live.

foregrounds.what: Body copy on a card.
Secondary copy, column headers, the not-judged label.
Hairlines and dashed marks only.
CDE identifiers, DOIs, outbound references.
The secondary accent, light-surface form.
adopt / approved / judged coherent.
refine / split / qualify — the coherence flag, the most important signal on Gate 1.
The destructive TEXT register.
The destructive FILL hue, also used as a text colour. Thin margin by construction — never tint it further.
The informational register, folded into the action accent.

The accent as a GLYPH or emphasised figure on paper — a card-title icon, an active label. Same value as --link-on-raised and a different statement: a title icon is not a link, and calling it one is the lie `ph-navy` was.

surfaces.what: The page field the raised surfaces sit on — the navy GROUND (UI-SPEC 5.1: dark page, cream cards). Its foregrounds were the gap that motivated this whole layer: no anchor covered text-on-field, so the field inherited the CHROME's foreground and bare copy rendered cream-on-cream while the contrast gate stayed green. Now the pair moves together or not at all.

foregrounds.what: Bare copy directly on the field. AAA-body, not AAA: the field carries running copy (page headers, section leads, standing notes) exactly as the chrome does, so it is held to the same 13:1 the other body surface is. 13.86:1.
Secondary copy on the field — a page subtitle, a standing caveat. 7.23:1.
Hairlines and separator glyphs on the field. 4.04:1, deliberately inside the non-text band.

A link on the field IS the foreground colour. The accent measures 2.47:1 on the ground and is prohibited (5.2), so this is the one field role that is not a mechanical copy of the chrome pair — it is the same DECISION the chrome made, re-made.

surfaces.what: Header bands, row hover, inset panels INSIDE a raised surface. Same value as the field today and a different role on purpose — an inset sits inside a card, a field sits under one.

foregrounds.what: Copy in a table header band or a hovered row.
Secondary copy in an inset panel.
A link in an inset panel.

surfaces.what: The SECOND inset step: pressed, selected, a badge fill. An interaction has two states — hover is a hint, pressed is a commitment — and one step cannot say both. Collapsing the two is how a button stops acknowledging the click.

foregrounds.what: Copy on a pressed control or a badge fill.
Secondary copy on that fill — a toast's description line.

The accent as a label on the fill. It measures 5.03:1 and it is ONLY legal because the step stayed at 6% — at 10% it is 4.65:1 and at 12% it is sub-AA. This row is the assertion that keeps the step light enough to carry it.

surfaces.what: The well a coverage/verdict bar is drawn in. A bar and its track are a (surface, foreground) pair like any other, and asserting it is what forced --series-residual from 55% to 62%: 55% clears the graphical floor against PAPER (3.16:1) but only 2.97:1 against the track it is actually drawn in, and the tighter of two constraints is the one that decides the value.

foregrounds.what: Probed as `text-` because the gate reads a foreground as `color`; the bar itself is painted with `bg-on-track`, which is the SAME `--color-on-track` key, so proving one proves the other. The achromatic bar itself — the residual mark, aliased so the two are one value rather than two neutrals half a step apart.

surfaces.what: The single primary action per screen. It is a SURFACE when filled, so it carries a bound foreground like any other.

foregrounds.what: The label inside a filled primary action.

surfaces.what: The primary action under the pointer. A hover is a SURFACE with its own bound label, not an opacity trick — dropping the button's alpha would show the field through it.

foregrounds.what: The same label, on the hovered fill. It can only improve on the base (5.61 -> 6.55) because the fill darkens toward the paper ink.
The label on the pressed fill (7.73:1).
The label inside a filled destructive action.

surfaces.what: A destructive action under the pointer.

foregrounds.what: The label on the hovered destructive fill (5.75:1). The base is the thinnest margin in the system at 4.62:1, so the hover state is where it gets room.
The label on the pressed destructive fill (7.09:1).

surfaces.what: The wash a success badge sits on.

foregrounds.what: The badge's own label.

surfaces.what: The wash the coherence flag and the site-wide caveat band sit on.

foregrounds.what: The flag's own label.

surfaces.what: The wash a destructive status label sits on.

foregrounds.what: The label's own text.

surfaces.what: The wash an informational callout sits on.

foregrounds.what: The callout's own text.

graphicalMarks.note: Charts live on raised surfaces. Each step is a graphical object, so 3:1 is the floor, not 4.5:1.

prohibited.why: UI-SPEC 5.2, the hard rule: the accent never touches the chrome. It measures 2.47:1. On the chrome an action is outlined in a paper-alpha rule with the chrome's own foreground.
UI-SPEC 5.4: the dark-surface form of the secondary accent never touches a raised surface (2.51:1). Use --accent-2-on-raised.

UI-SPEC 5.2, THE hard rule, now binding on the field too: blue never touches the ground, and the field IS the ground. 2.47:1. This row is what makes the flip a checkable act rather than a claim — before it, the accent on the field was legal (5.70:1 on cream-dim) and nothing would have objected to a blue link surviving the flip into illegibility.

The MIRROR of the pre-flip row this replaces. While the field was light, the prohibited pairing was the dark-surface teal on it; now the field is dark, it is the light-surface teal that is prohibited (2.93:1). The prohibition encodes a RELATIONSHIP — the wrong form of the accent for the surface — and the relationship is what survives a surface change.

The paper ink on the navy field: 1.04:1, and the exact mirror of the cream-on-cream defect this plan was written for. An unmigrated component that kept `text-on-raised` while the field moved lands here, so the prohibition names the failure mode rather than trusting the migration to have been complete.
